description: Verify that DUT reassembles a 2-fragment Echo Request and emits an Echo Reply whose Identifier, Sequence Number, and Data match the reassembled Request — basic in-order reassembly (RFC 791 §3.2 + RFC 1122 §3.3.2)
approach:
[Objective]
The foundational reassembly case: split an Echo Request across two IP fragments (frag 0 carries first half + IP header; frag 1 carries second half), send in order, expect DUT to reassemble and echo back the full content.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Tester → DUT: IPv4 fragment 0 (offset=0, MF=1, half of an Echo Request payload + ICMP header)
2. Tester → DUT: IPv4 fragment 1 (offset=N, MF=0, second half of the payload)
   ⇒ DUT must reassemble using shared (id, src, dst, protocol).

3. Observation (3 s window):
   • DUT → Tester: Echo Reply
      - identifier matches the original request
      - sequence matches
      - data matches the full reassembled payload

[Pass condition]
Reply received with matching id, seq, and data.

[Fail condition]
• Fail_echo_id — Reply identifier did not match
• Fail_echo_seq — Reply sequence did not match
• Fail_data_mismatch — Reply data differed from reassembled payload
• Fail_timeout — DUT did not emit a Reply within the window

verdicts.Pass: DUT reassembled and echoed back full Echo Request — normal reassembly
verdicts.Fail_echo_id: Reply identifier did not match Request
verdicts.Fail_echo_seq: Reply sequence did not match Request
verdicts.Fail_data_mismatch: Reply data differed from reassembled payload
verdicts.Fail_timeout: DUT did not emit a Reply within the window
